$comment: Project-level permissions for the Release Management workflows.
Almost everything here is read-only or writes only to scratch space. Generalized on purpose:
the per-invocation entries that accumulate in settings.local.json (exact curl strings, one
chmod per file) never match the next command and so never stop the prompting.
ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION: the `python3 -c` and `python3 - <<` entries pre-approve arbitrary
Python, which is not read-only. An audit of 528 Bash calls across five sessions found ad-hoc
analysis snippets were the single largest source of prompts (~196 segments), and the only
alternative was every user granting it locally and diverging. This is a project settings file,
so the grant applies only while working inside this repo -- that scope is what makes it
acceptable. Note the same caveat already applied to `sed`, `awk`, `echo` and `cat`, any of
which can write through a shell redirect.
Deliberately NOT allowed: git commit/push/reset, bare curl, and any write to the
working tree outside scripts/ and reference/.

A compound command needs EVERY segment allowed: a permitted script piped through grep or head still prompts, which is why the read-only text utilities are listed. curl entries appear twice because prefix matching is literal and quoted URLs do not match an unquoted entry.

No Gecko-checkout entries live here on purpose. This file is shared and the clone path is per-machine, so a literal path in it is wrong for everyone but its author. The checkout path is resolved once by `watchlist.py check-setup`, stored per-user, and the matching Bash(git -C <path> ...) entries are written to the git-ignored settings.local.json. Run check-setup on a new machine or the gecko reads will prompt on every call.

SYNTAX NOTE: entries whose prefix ends mid-argument use the glob form `Bash(prefix*)`, not `Bash(prefix:*)`. Observed 2026-08-05: `Bash(python3 scripts/relnotes/:*)` did NOT stop prompts for `python3 scripts/relnotes/daily-pass.py ...` while a blanket `Bash(python3 *)` did, and the entries that worked all end at a token boundary (`git log:*`, `grep:*`). So `:*` appears to match only where the prefix ends a whole argument; a prefix ending in `/` never matches. Do not convert these back to `:*`.
